ateret-zekenim/2:א: If a non-Jew brings, etc. — and if the non-Jew accepted not in the Jew's presence, it is permitted after Passover because he wants the leniency to acquire and the prohibition does not want to acquire — so too the Jew did not intend to acquire chametz on Pesach until after yom tov (responsum of Rashba).
ateret-zekenim/3:_: To a non-Jew outside the house, etc. — this certainly has no taste or smell, for it is worse that the chametz is in his house; and further Terumat HaDeshen did not write outside the house — implying he spoke of the chametz being outside the house, and we are not concerned about the non-Jew even if in his servant's house, for below he permits even one who recognizes him and is accustomed, etc. All this I wrote per Beit Yosef in the name of Terumat HaDeshen; but the essence of the matter appears in the Gemara daf 6 — he designated a house for the non-Jew's chametz, he need not burn — we learn even in a Jew's house it helps to designate a corner; only Terumat HaDeshen did not come to exclude designating a corner, for that is also called outside the Jew's house; and it is obvious the chametz should be placed where the gentile can enter himself — all the more not.
beur-hagra/1:_: Seif 1 permitted even. Yerushalmi there — Rosh brought there; and Gemara 1a: go out and buy, etc.; and there 1b: shops of gentiles, etc.
beur-hagra/2:_: Seif 2 he should not, etc. — and also, etc., and it is good. For perforce he does not acquire his domain, as in Bava Metzia 117a — the reason is their faces, etc.; but on the first part one does not listen — no challenge; and even without saying, stam we do not acquire his domain, as written 96b daf 2: leniency, etc., and there 102a, and Chullin 139a: wherever he, etc.; and this is what "it is good" means — for clarity; but if the Jew accepts, even though it is a prohibition, it acquires for him, as in Avodah Zarah 42a: perhaps he will lift it, etc.; and this is why he wrote he should not, etc., and likewise his domain, as in chapter 6 of Demai: convert and gentile, etc.; and if they come, etc.; and this is why he also wrote he should not — for domain acquires immediately when he desires it, as in Bava Batra chapter 5: in the buyer's domain, once, etc.
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3 even if he left it. Meaning do not say the penalty does not apply to R' Shimon — proof from Israel who pledged with a gentile, forbidden if he did not say from now — there 1a; nevertheless.
beur-hagra/3:ב: And if he sold, etc. Tosefta and Yerushalmi chapter 2 halacha 2.
beur-hagra/3:ג: Outside the house. Terumat HaDeshen; Magen Avraham; Magen Avraham in siman 449 seif 5; and resolved Taz's difficulty; and see end.
beur-hagra/3:ד: Even though, etc. There; and he brings proof from what is written in Gittin 22: Rami bar Chama asked, etc., learn: even he, etc., rather, etc.; and see Rashi s.v. rather, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ו: Without, etc. Rambam; and as explained on the Tosefta: provided, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ז: Or that he sell, etc. As Maharam; and Agudah in Tosefta: until you acquire for two hundred take for one hundred and I will buy from you after Pesach — meaning even if he tells him to acquire expensively and give him profit, it is permitted since he sells without evasion (Bach).
beur-hagra/3:ח: But a gift. As the Gemara explains in that Tosefta: provided, etc.; and even though elsewhere it works because of chametz stringency (Hagahot Maimoniyot).
beur-hagra/5:_: Seif 5 chametz. Yerushalmi in hefker; Or Zarua; and see siman 436 seif 1 in the gloss.
beur-hagra/7:_: Seif 7 forbidden to give, etc. And specifically chametz; and as Yerushalmi there: if for his dog it is benefit prohibition; see Tosafot chapter 2 of Pesachim 22b s.v. and a limb, etc.
biur-halacha/1:_: Chametz of a non-Jew — and if it was under Jewish liability its law was explained in siman 440; see there.
biur-halacha/3:א: Chametz of a Jew — and regarding stolen chametz over which Passover passed, whether permitted to the victim — see Noda BiYehudah Orach Chayim siman 20 who leaned to permit; Acharonim disagree, as explained in Ittur section on biur chametz daf 125, Ramban chapter Kol Sha'ah, Ritva, and Maharam Chalavah there — all derive from the sugya of the robber that it is forbidden to everyone; already some Acharonim raised from Ramban's words; however regarding robbery of a gentile — Jew's chametz over which Passover passed — Ateret Rosh leaned to permit; Pri Megadim and Maharit Algazi copied.
biur-halacha/3:ג: Even if he left by mistake or under duress — see Mishna Berurah. Mechaber wrote anonymously and did not explain whether when through mistake or duress he did not burn and also did not nullify — therefore forbidden; but if he nullified though he did not check because of duress, permitted since at least the essence of the law d'oraisa was fulfilled; or even if he nullified and left without burning because of duress, also forbidden — Acharonim dispute; see below seif 5 regarding nullification — for stringent view there, certainly here where he did not check at all though under duress; but per lenient view there, one can say likewise here even without checking, since under duress it is no worse than checked, nullified, and found after Pesach; so in Torat HaShelamim.
biur-halacha/3:ד: And if he sold — see Mishna Berurah that if he left a seal on the chametz at sale time, even b'dieved forbidden; see Pri Megadim who leans this is specifically in a small sale — selling all chametz for a small amount — for then it is void sale, and leniency is only because truly the chametz is not in his domain since Torah forbade benefit and Scripture placed it in his domain for bal yera'eh; therefore whoever reveals he does not want them and is pleased they leave his domain, even for a small amount suffices; and therefore whoever leaves a seal beforehand appears not to want the sale — unlike our sales where we make a proper deed for each measure for such-and-such sum and add extra money as a loan and the chametz is his.
biur-halacha/3:ה: Provided he gives — see Mishna Berurah there is no agency for a gentile, even gentile to gentile — from Magen Avraham and Sha'agat Aryeh, unlike Mishna Berurah and Shach Choshen Mishpat siman 243; see Mateh Yehuda who expanded — when chametz was already brought to the gentile sender's house, certainly the sale stands since with the seller's knowledge it was brought to the buyer gentile's house and the gentile knowingly received in his house, and the agent's act does not detract, for he is like a monkey (see there); he concludes even if the agent were a Jew, all agree we say no agency for a gentile — nevertheless it helps for the reason stated; and it is obvious his words apply only if he brought chametz to the buyer's house — but per our custom we transfer.
biur-halacha/3:ו: Absolute sale — Rav Bnei Yeshua siman 2 letter 5 wrote: since selling chametz to a gentile must be absolute without evasion, it appears after Pesach when the gentile returns chametz to the Jew he must acquire by one of the acquisitions and not merely receive back — as poskim wrote regarding gift on condition to return siman 258; it appears after Pesach it suffices to acquire chametz and rooms from the gentile with money alone and the gentile returns the sale deed — for though a Jew does not acquire land from a gentile with money alone without a deed, there he does not rely — unlike here where he returns the deed (end of his words).
biur-halacha/3:ז: For a small amount — see Mishna Berurah; today all Israel's custom is not to sell for a small amount but for a price close to chametz value, and they take from the gentile some gold (called auf gab) as initial payment and add the rest as a loan, as explained in Choshen Mishpat siman 190 — this works. Acharonim wrote: beware not to raise the price much above value in a large sum lest it be void sale; Pri Megadim implies therefore b'dieved it does not block since by their law he cannot retract; and implies if that place's custom is to retract for void sale it blocks — requires study. Further wrote it does not work when he says: I sell you this house or my chametz.
biur-halacha/3:ט: Does not work — this law is from Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 6 of Shabbat; he inferred this law from Tosefta (see there); Terumat HaDeshen siman 120 brings it and it appears there l'chatchila permitted even to practice so; in truth requires study — for l'chatchila certainly forbidden by law since he attached his gift to a condition, and when the condition is not fulfilled he does not return retroactively and it is his chametz — he enters doubt in d'oraisa bal yera'eh, especially when the condition depends on others lest so-and-so not fulfill; I found in Machaneh Ephraim Laws of Forbidden Foods he wrote l'chatchila certainly forbidden for the reason we wrote; but the poskim's language.
chatam-sofer/3:_: A gentile who sold a Jew's chametz through agency — since there is no agency for a gentile, the owners violate bal yera'eh (see Ketzot HaChoshen siman 226 s.k. 15, end of his words).
chatam-sofer/4:_: (there in Magen Avraham s.k. 4) But gentile to gentile works. I would say: see Shach Choshen Mishpat siman 243 s.k. 5 and Beit Shmuel there.
chatam-sofer/6:_: (there s.v.) And what he wrote we follow, etc. in Avodah Zarah daf 71 in Tosafot. I would say: s.v. Ameimar said, etc. — since they needed to say it is only an excuse, we learn we do not follow when he regrets; and further they needed acquisition of place in firstborn (see there); nevertheless examine well responsum attributed to Ramban siman 225 and you will find satisfaction.
chatam-sofer/7:_: (there in Magen Avraham) s.v. However one must, etc., and siman 43. I would say: examine well above what Taz wrote siman 426 s.k. 5 and what Taz wrote below end of this siman; examine well in responsa Chasam Sofer Orach Chayim siman 84.
chok-yaakov/1:ב: Non-Jew — it appears one who has partnership with a gentile in chametz over which Passover passed — even though half belonging to a Jew is forbidden in benefit — nevertheless when he divides after Pesach with the gentile, the gentile's share is permitted in benefit as gentile's chametz law, and we do not say there is no clarification, since chametz over which Passover passed is only forbidden d'rabbanan as a penalty and there is no d'oraisa root — we say there is clarification (for eating requires study; see above siman 457) as in chapter Meshilin (Beitzah 38a); see Yam Shel Shlomo Bava Kamma chapter 5 siman 32 on laws of clarification; but the Jew's share is certainly forbidden, for even partners' chametz is forbidden in benefit, as above siman 445 (see there).
chok-yaakov/1:ג: Even for eating. So is agreed from the Talmud and all poskim; but Tur brought in the name of Ittur that his view is to be stringent — a mere fence as Tur himself concluded; likewise in Sefer Tanya and Shibolei Leket general 7 siman 62 in the name of Baal HaDevarim explicitly like Ittur, as a mere fence; it appears Baal Ittur is Baal HaDevarim, as in Sanhedrin 49; likewise in Shita Mekubetzet both authored Rivash; and though for law all poskim agree not to be stringent, and Shita Leket itself — nevertheless I wrote all this because I saw Bach left Ittur's words in doubt from several sugyot and Taz forces to reconcile; in truth initially no difficulty.
chok-yaakov/2:ג: On the last day of Pesach. For emphasis it states the last day — even so he should not accept the chametz from him — likewise responsum Rashba siman 171; but in truth this applies to the first days; good that he spoke in present tense, for custom is to bring gifts on the last day from minchah upward as Tur in the name of Ittur; see responsum Nachalat Sheva who wrote: emphasis on last day — on first days since d'oraisa prohibition is obvious we say he does not want a prohibition fixed for him (end of his words). If last yom tov — no covering vessel or ten-handbreadth partition, for they did not fear brief eating; during Pesach need covering as above; likewise if gentile forgot chametz with Jew — same as gift here.
chok-yaakov/2:ו: And good that he say he does not want — so if the gentile takes it after Pesach it will not prove retroactively his intent during Pesach was to acquire; nevertheless if he did not say so, permitted by law even in his guarded courtyard — he does not acquire against his will, for he does not want prohibition acquired. All this is gift without Jewish liability; if gentile brings to sell or deposit, Jew must explicitly refuse acceptance and liability; even if not liable by law but knows gentile is violent and will compel payment — forbidden, as siman 440 (end of his words).
chok-yaakov/7:ב: That it is chametz. Avnei Nezer wrote b'dieved permitted like a cow fattened with gentile barley refuse, as Yoreh De'ah siman 142 (end of his words); possibly not comparable, since his animal ate gentile chametz forbidden in benefit during Pesach — he benefits from chametz; nevertheless he must cast benefit-value to loss for what was necessary for his animal; regarding cow of gentile it is obvious; here cast at least value of benefit the Jew had from what his animal ate, to sea or sell all to gentile except prohibition value — as one who benefits from forbidden benefit; careful reader at end of chapter Kol HaGoyim will see b'dieved permitted entirely for this reason — this and that cause — requires study.
chok-yaakov/4:ב: And I will take from you. Responsum Rashba siman 499 concludes: I or another Jew will take it from you; see responsum Maharam Bava Batra siman 91; Acharonim wrote he should say and I will give you profit afterward.
dagul-merevavah/1:_: In my view it is preferable that among acquisition methods the gentile acquire chametz through chalipin (sudar-kinyan); what can I do — Shach in Choshen Mishpat siman 123 s.k. 30 objected to this.
chok-yaakov/2:א: If a gentile brings — Beit Hillel wrote Yoreh De'ah siman 332 seif 1: When I was in Hamburg I was asked about a Jew who before Pesach had grain in a gentile's mill; the grain remained until chol hamoed; on the seventh day the gentile ground the Jew's grain, made bread, baked, and brought the bread immediately after Pesach — the gentile thought he did the Jew a favor bringing ready bread; I was asked the law since chametz of a Jew was made through a gentile during Pesach. I answered permitted to take the money for that bread from the gentile, and that gentile may eat or sell to another gentile.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: Gift of chametz. If a gentile gave or sold wheat etc. to a Jew and he accepted, and after Pesach it became known there was chametz inside — l'chatchila it appears the chametz is permitted after Pesach as gentile's chametz; proof from Nedarim 35: one who said my loaves are konam to you — who transgressed? The recipient can say: I wanted leniency, not prohibition — Rashi, Ran, and Rosh explain unintentional misuse; but one who takes hekdesh money unintentionally misuses even if he would not have wanted to acquire had he known, since he himself took to acquire; but what another gave him.
chok-yaakov/2:ד: The Jew should not accept. If he transgressed and accepted — Tur's implication in the name of Ittur: forbidden even in benefit after Pesach; and it must be that even last yom tov is d'rabbanan and d'oraisa he did not violate — nevertheless whatever Sages enacted like d'oraisa they enacted, and lest one be lenient on second yom tov — requires study.
chok-yaakov/2:ה: He should not show through his actions. It appears when he did not say: place it on a rock or bring from the river, etc. — even though explained in first chapter of Kiddushin and Avnei Nezer siman 40 that a woman who said these expressions for betrothal is not betrothed, because there we need revealed intent to accept for kiddushin, and saying these expressions shows she does not want kiddushin — unlike here where we need that he not desire chametz at all — clear; see responsum Maharam Mintz siman 82.
chok-yaakov/3:ד: To a gentile. Taz wrote even if he is his servant (end of his words) — when he is not his Canaanite slave; likewise responsum Sha'ar Ephraim part 1 siman 3 it is like his own; he wrote: do not reject because leniency wants to acquire and prohibition does not — end of his words; he did not write from what reason not to reject; but it is simple: a slave's hand is his master's hand — it never left his domain even if he transfers to the slave, for it is his hand and domain for acquisition; likewise for eruv acquisitions (Eruvin 59b). Not comparable to Yoreh De'ah siman 169 gloss seif 9 — per those who hold no agency for gentiles, permitted to give to his slave and maidservant neighbors.
chok-yaakov/3:ה: Outside the house. So in Terumat HaDeshen siman 119 and 128 — intent to place his chametz outside his house; likewise Acharonim wrote the reason: otherwise it is like depositing with a Jew; therefore they challenged this law and wrote it is a mere stringency; in my humble opinion Terumat HaDeshen's reason is simple: otherwise how does the gentile acquire the gift since he did not pull chametz from Jewish domain? Terumat HaDeshen deals with gift; even in sale to a gentile he does not acquire with money but pulling, as Yoreh De'ah siman 317 and Tosafot gentiles in the name of Rabbenu Tam — their acquisition is essentially pulling, for we hold d'oraisa money acquires for a Jew — "to your fellow" with money, for gentile with pulling, as chapter 2 of Bekhorot; Rosh there; likewise Maggid Mishneh chapter 1 of laws.
chok-yaakov/3:ו: Absolute gift. Even through his agent or wife he can transfer chametz; we do not say a woman is worse at transferring something that returns to her afterward, as the Gemara concludes in Gittin 19 (see there). Responsum Chinuch Beit Yehuda siman 13 brought an incident: one had chametz and wanted to sell to a gentile properly; he schemed not to tell the gentile vessels of his chametz but left it in a friend's room knowing the friend would sell that room with his chametz inside to the gentile and gave the key; the friend sold the room and the hidden chametz was sold with the room's chametz without the selling Jew or buying gentile knowing — he ruled the other Jew's chametz forbidden (see there).
chok-yaakov/3:ח: Gift on condition to return does not work — only because of chametz stringency; they did not add to compare to another matter. Magen Avraham wrote: all the more if he said I give you and you return them to me — it is an absolute gift permitted by law, only stringency of chametz to be stringent (end Magen Avraham). His words are very astonishing — on the contrary, Yoreh De'ah siman 305 seif 8 gloss ruled a gentile who said and you return them to me is not a gift at all — responsum of Rashba siman 198: specifically on condition that is like from now it is a gift, unlike if he said and you return them to me; see Rashba siman 286 — requires study.
chok-yaakov/4:א: Until you acquire chametz for a maneh — Rambam's language chapter 4 of chametz laws: until you acquire from a gentile, acquire from a Jew.
chok-yaakov/5:א: Forbidden even though he nullified — we fear evasion that he will say he nullified though he did not, since he acted not as Sages required — not burning or selling to a gentile; even though now all nullify, we fear evasion; even absolute hefker — law is so; even witnesses of hefker and nullification do not help if he left chametz in his house knowingly all Pesach — certainly nullification or hefker does not help; but whenever he did not know all Pesach and witnesses nullified or declared hefker before Pesach, or absolute coercion in sale and all Pesach he thought he sold and after Pesach learned he did not because coerced — so great coercion he said.
chok-yaakov/5:ב: Even though he nullified. L'chatchila it would appear per sugya Moed Katan 13: where he violated d'oraisa they penalized his son after him, unlike d'rabbanan — if so when he nullified chametz and died, his chametz should be permitted in benefit to his son since they did not penalize the son when there is no d'oraisa violation; but this is not per Ran's reason who forbids feeding chametz after Pesach even to others' animals — for the Sages penalized not him who violated but everyone (end of his words) — requires study.
chok-yaakov/7:א: To feed during Pesach days. So Beit Yosef; also in Hagahot Agudah — responsum Maharil siman 191; in Agudah itself: one may not tell a gentile take my animal in your house and feed it chametz, but stam give it to graze those Pesach days (end of his words) — implies only if he explicitly says feed chametz it is forbidden; but stam even if he certainly knows he will feed chametz, permitted per his view, like the law of telling one's slave, etc. (see there) — all in one basket; l'chatchila do not be lenient.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1 chametz of a gentile, etc. I will copy here several novelties very needed for law, with God's help. (1) An incident came: one had chametz needed for royal tax; because he did not pay as required, the king's officers took the chametz to the tax treasury and the matter went to court, doubtful whether all chametz would be forfeited to the king or the Jew would prove his right and win to return the chametz; now the questioner asked what to do on Pesach with this chametz in the king's house and whether sale to a gentile helps — requires study whether sale to a gentile helps at all, for.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (there seif 2) If a gentile brings a Jew a gift, etc. We learn in Talmud first chapter of Chullin: Rava said — a baraita supports you: chametz of sinners is permitted immediately because they exchange. They thought: whose view is R' Yehuda who holds chametz over which Passover passed is forbidden from the Torah? How was it not established perhaps Rabbanan? It appears per what we learn in Sheviit chapter 5 mishnah 5: from when may one buy turnips after shemittah? R' Yehuda: immediately; Chachamim: when the new increases — if so proven for Rabbanan we do not rely on leniency though not established there for sinners; likewise this presumption that they do not abandon.
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (there seif 3) Jew's chametz over which Passover passed forbidden in benefit, etc. I copy several notes and legal novelties. [1] I was asked: one owed a woman money and would not pay; when she pressed him as she needed to marry, he pitied her and gave chametz as pledge for the debt; the third party held the chametz on condition: if the match concludes as she said, the third party gives her the chametz; if not, returns to him; now the match did not conclude and the borrower wants his chametz and the woman withholds since she is owed — meanwhile Pesach arrived and the woman.
chokhmat-shlomo/4:_: (there seif 5) Chametz found in a Jew's house after Pesach forbidden, etc. In law: if one robbed chametz on the eve after six before night, whether permitted in benefit after Pesach — see my work Avodat Avodah on Avodah Zarah 72 Tosafot s.v. what about restoration — we wrote there a new leniency not considered by Rishonim; explained there whether pulling acquisition applies d'oraisa to chametz for a Jew (see there) — good reasoning, examine. Whether permitted to sell chametz to a Jew suspected of sins and the buyer will sell after — see responsum to community Tarnopol in laws of Eruvin siman 366 incidentally (see there); also pilpul and explanation of the sugya Rish.
chokhmat-shlomo/5:_: (there seif 7) Forbidden to give his animal to a gentile to feed during Pesach, etc. In law: selling animals on Pesach to eat chametz — Tosafot Shabbat forbids because evasion does not work for Torah law; I expanded elsewhere; now I found explicit proof for Tosafot Shabbat — evasion does not work for Torah law in chapter 3 of Pesachim Yerushalmi halacha 3: his view changed — R' Yehuda there said permitted to evade; here he said forbidden to evade; R' said: here rabbinic, there karet liability — see Korban HaEdah; if so proven like rabbinic evasion is permitted, not Torah — main point per second explanation of Korban HaEdah: if he bakes it is lashes, proven evasion forbidden on Shabbat as Tosafot Shabbat — this is proof.
dagul-merevavah/2:_: Explanation: and you return it to me after Pesach — it follows all Pesach days it is an absolute gift, unlike Yoreh De'ah siman 305 seif 8: telling a kohen take five selas and return them to me — he did not complete the gift even one hour (see there); Taz s.k. 7 what he wrote in the name of Perishah and Shach s.k. 8; Chak Yakov challenged Magen Avraham in vain.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] Of Samaritans, etc. One who has partnership with Samaritans in chametz over which Passover passed — when he divides after Pesach, his share is forbidden in benefit and the Samaritan's share permitted in benefit, for there is clarification in d'rabbanan; for eating requires study (Chak Yakov); see Yoreh De'ah siman 146 seif 4: convert and Samaritans who inherited Samaritan fathers — the convert can tell the Samaritan take your idolatry and I take money, etc., because convert inheritance is d'rabbanan; but if they partnered, forbidden; if so here likewise for chametz; however there the reason is he wants its existence (see Tosafot Avodah Zarah 64); if so likewise if partnership in chametz and money — forbidden; however chametz does not bind its value (see end siman 443). Incident.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] Even for eating, etc. Per this one must say what Eruvin 64 teaches — Samaritan chametz after Pesach permitted in benefit — because forbidden in eating due to Samaritan bread; now Rashi and Tosafot's need for Samaritan bread reason is resolved.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] Gift of chametz, etc. Likewise lost Samaritan chametz with a Jew (Chak Yakov). Rokeach siman 297 on Pesach: one cannot accept any chametz deposit — until here; it implies even if explained without liability and designated place — permitted before Pesach as siman 440 and Rama responsum 177 — not so l'chatchila.
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [6] [Levush] and Samaritans, etc. Even his servant (Bach and Taz), unlike his Canaanite slave and maidservant — his hand is his master's (Sha'ar Ephraim); likewise to Samaritan apostate one may not sell, for though he sinned he is a Jew. Incident: sold burnt wine for a large sum, hard to lose — close the Jew would not comply; I said the Samaritan apostate should exchange with another Samaritan and take other burnt wine, then permitted to the Jew, or sell and money permitted to ask — chametz does not bind its value (Taz); see end siman 463. In responsum printed end Sha'ar Ephraim I wondered on Sha'ar Ephraim siman 4 who permitted the burnt wine itself after.
eshel-avraham/4:_: He transgresses. Pri Chadash wrote this per view of siman 440 (see there) that is the main point. Gift on condition to return — if on condition you do such-and-such, this is absolute sale. See Choshen Mishpat siman 212 seif 2 and Avnei Nezer siman 28; however because of chametz stringency forbidden; see seif 3.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Chametz of a gentile, etc. Yerushalmi chapter Kol Sha'ah: convert died and left chametz over which Passover passed — whoever precedes after Pesach and acquires, permitted per his view (end of his words). This does not contradict our Talmud Bava Kamma 110b — robbing convert's chametz over which Passover passed forbidden in benefit — there the convert did not die until chametz prohibition applied, or even if he died before Pesach, it was in the robber's hand during chametz prohibition — unlike here when the convert died the chametz remained ownerless, so no one violates bal yera'eh of yours — you see of hefker. Kaf HaChayyim 1; Mekor Chayyim 1; Chayei Adam general 124 24. If so likewise hefker chametz permitted after.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There. Chametz of a gentile, etc. — the whole world practiced leniency with gentile chametz over which Passover passed and none is careful; but of a Jew, even if nullified, forbidden in benefit (Radbaz responsum part 1 siman 485; Birkei Yosef 1) — meaning to exclude Baal Ittur as below letter 7 (see there); also see below seif 5.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There. Chametz of a gentile, etc. One who has partnership with a gentile in chametz over which Passover passed — even though half of a Jew is forbidden in benefit, when he divides after Pesach the gentile's share is permitted in benefit, since chametz over which Passover passed is only forbidden d'rabbanan as penalty we say there is clarification (for eating requires study; however in Chok HaPesach 1 s.v. it appears permitted even for eating — see there; likewise Razah). But the Jew's share is certainly forbidden in benefit (Kaf HaChayyim 2; Ateret Rosh 1; Yad Ephraim 1; Mekor Chayyim 1; Razah 27; Chayei Adam there 25; see Mekor Chayyim who leans the gentile's share is permitted specifically when placed in the gentile's house).
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (4) Jew and gentile partnered in chametz and other things — forbidden to tell the gentile: you take chametz and I take other things (Mekor Chayyim 3; Chayei Adam there). However Ateret Rosh there appears lenient because chametz does not bind its value (see there); and possible in great loss one may rely on this.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There. Permitted even for eating. That which the Mishnah teaches (Pesachim 28a) gentile chametz over which Passover passed permitted in benefit — not to imply forbidden in eating; rather because it needed to teach Jew's forbidden in benefit, it taught regarding gentile permitted in benefit (Rif and Rosh). In the name of Yerushalmi Rosh wrote: Mishnah gentile chametz permitted in benefit — where they did not practice eating gentile bread; but where practiced, permitted even in eating (Beit Din, Beit Yosef; Razah 2). See Yoreh De'ah siman 112 seif 2 which gentile bread they were lenient (see there).
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (7) There. Permitted even in eating — so proven from Talmud, etc., as previous letter; but Tur brought in the name of Baal Ittur forbidden in eating — already wrote above letter 2 that the whole world practiced leniency (see there).
levushei-serad/1:_: Shulchan Aruch seif 2: if a gentile brings a Jew a gift of chametz, etc. — see Simchat Yom Tov daf 5.
levushei-serad/2:_: See there seif 3 over which Passover passed forbidden in benefit, etc. — law of nullification; see Magen Avraham siman 447 s.k. 44; Pri Megadim Orach Chayim first section siman 69 s.k. 17 (see there).
levushei-serad/7:_: There even though he nullified, etc. — see Mishna Berurah siman 58 and Netivei Yisrael siman 14.
peri-megadim/1:_: Permitted (Taz). Bach challenged from baraita 41b; Pri Chadash challenged from seif 4 from Tosefta that one may tell a gentile; and Pesachim 1a: go out and acquire chametz of soldiers. Taz explained everything; one can say for Chizkiyah who does not eat leaven within its time — before its time permitted in benefit, only in eating; nevertheless for R' Yehuda in Tosafot Pesachim 28b s.v. one; Rif and Rosh appear they ruled like Chizkiyah — R' Eliezer Pesachim chapter 8 not like R' Meir (Pri Megadim chapter 8 from Magen Avraham letter 5). In Gemara 29a it challenges: if R' Yehuda, gentile's too — R' Avahu challenges; for Chizkiyah one can answer: Mishnah — R' Yehuda: gentile's permitted after Pesach in benefit, in eating forbidden; nevertheless Jew's forbidden — penalty too; Beit Yosef rules like R' Yehuda and these baraitot like R' Shimon; what Beit Yosef rules like R' Shimon before its time — Tur in his name in Pri Megadim — one can say after its time he ruled like R' Yehuda, for for us too before its time like R' Yehuda and after like R' Shimon; Pesachim 28b implies from when forbidden in eating forbidden in benefit like R' Yehuda — a fortiori from orlah not worked as sin — see Peri Chadash; however after Pesach permitted in eating also for R' Shimon — nevertheless no a fortiori from orlah as stated. What Bach wrote: one must check within the festival and after the festival will be explained in letter 7; in Magen Avraham 8. Gentile chametz during Pesach forbidden in benefit, for we do not hold like Rav Acha (Beit Yosef; Pri Chadash); therefore forbidden to smell gentile bread (see Eruvin 64b; Tur what Beit Yosef wrote: nullified after Pesach forbidden in eating and permitted in benefit — no reason, etc.). And what Taz wrote: even hefker forbidden in eating and permitted in benefit for R' Yehuda and Chizkiyah — requires study; see letter 3.
peri-megadim/2:_: Yom tov (Taz) — b'dieved even first yom tov permitted even stam, for he does not want a prohibition to be acquired (end of his words). On the eighth day if he accepted — forbidden in benefit (Ateret Rosh; Levush 63) even though expert in lunar fixation and did not violate bal yera'eh — nevertheless they made a fence; in all places day 2 like day 1. If accepted on second yom tov day 1 — l'chatchila after Pesach rabbinic doubt lenient; one can say the prohibition was established as siman 442 Magen Avraham 1; Magen Avraham here 1; see a fortiori; Kaf HaChayyim; letter 16 last yom tov need not cover vessel — why siman 446? There one day suffices with covering; in any case on last yom tov which is rabbinic lest one be lenient — it appears even stiff need cover — requires study; see what I wrote letter 3.
peri-megadim/3:א: And it is good (Taz) — b'dieved even silent, as long as he did not act — we say he does not want a prohibition to be acquired, even if it stands guarded there (end of his words).
peri-megadim/3:ב: And know that a man's courtyard — if he wants, he acquires even benefit prohibitions, as siman 446 and 447 — when a Jew lifts, he acquired. However stam eating prohibitions — owners presumably do not declare hefker; see Maharsha Beitzah 38b: stam eating prohibitions owners declare hefker — I stood in Pri Megadim 14; requires study; I doubt benefit prohibitions whether stam hefker or not — practical difference: convert with deposit with a Jew who died before night and the Jew said before death: acquire my courtyard for me — he died and afterward the Jew said he does not want to acquire before the convert died; per one view whoever did not violate only bal yimatzei — they did not penalize, as we want to say letter 6 letter 7 in Magen Avraham 3 — per view they penalized for violation — it can be envisioned in six that now if stam benefit prohibitions d'oraisa or d'rabbanan are hefker, the Jew already acquired and what he returned afterward cannot declare hefker again and he violated bal yera'eh and forbidden after Pesach; unlike if stam not hefker the Jew never acquired; since he returned before death it is not the Jew's and permitted after Pesach. I thought to learn from Yerushalmi chapter 9 of Sheviit: R' Chizkiyah went up to R' Yirmiyah, said I acquired my storehouses for me; he said carve these fruits for yourself; he said here is your place rented to me; he said not so, I declared them hefker; he returned and acquired them; Mahari Kra explained R' Chizkiyah said sheviit fruits at biur time Scripture declared hefker and he acquired, etc.; R' Yirmiyah said he rents his place and acquires for him; R' Chizkiyah said for us who did not declare hefker forbidden as biur time law (see there) — this can be rejected.
peri-megadim/4:א: To a gentile (Taz) — it must be only outside the house; b'dieved even without designating a corner, as long as he did not accept liability, permitted; l'chatchila they wrote one should sell the room too (Magen Avraham 4; and see there will be explained). Pri Megadim letter 13 in the name of Sha'agat Aryeh siman 3: one may not sell chametz to his Canaanite slave; Pri Megadim letter 6. Here too others sell for him; see Yoreh De'ah 267:17: without immersion his body is not acquired — nevertheless his handiwork and all his master's; practical difference only if he immersed to freedom; and so letter for Magen Avraham. Immersed — obviously violates bal yera'eh; possible also bal yimatzei until night; elsewhere we wrote from this; if one said to slave: I give you a gift on condition to return after Pesach.
peri-megadim/4:ג: Incident: one sold large barrels of burnt wine and left a seal after the sale — there is room to permit; even before sale our sale with proper deed each quart for such sum and the gentile if he wishes opens and does what he wants — only the seal until measurement — if so permitted, possible even l'chatchila; in Kaf HaChayyim he wrote because of evasion (Bach); this in small sale — void sale; only with revealed intent suffices per Rabbenu Chananel; whoever left seal beforehand appears not to want sale — unlike such a case as stated. Also what Bach wrote not to leave seal on the room — on barrels the gentile can sell to his fellow by pulling and measure after Pesach; Pri Megadim: gentile does not rely, unlike sale.
peri-megadim/4:ה: And know — an apostate who married a gentile woman, the child is a gentile, and the reverse child is Jewish — see Even HaEzer on this; b'dieved requires study — one can say better than an infant captured among gentiles, and you have no greater coercion; even coerced Jew forbidden — this is better; b'dieved if bought in absolute terms, one can say permitted. To sell to apostate woman to gentile l'chatchila no; if impossible with no other buyer, on condition she hold for herself and not sell even to her husband — as Taz letter 6 wrote, permitted.
peri-megadim/4:ד: And what he wrote one may not sell chametz to an apostate — apostate's chametz forbidden to all Israel (Ateret Rosh); likewise Choshen Mishpat part 1 law 4 and Chullin 4 chametz of sinners, etc.; Kaf HaChayyim letter 14: one may not buy after Pesach immediately from an apostate; possible doubt lest made after Pesach permitted (Kaf HaChayyim 449:1; Chullin 4:2 s.v. permitted; Maharsha there; and he said he speaks truth — even rabbinically he does not abandon leniency lest he anger — in Rosh Yosef we wrote there. However one can say l'chatchila doubt or rabbinic doubt — we do not act; see 110, 120: buying cooked things from gentiles stam bal yera'eh and doubt there from difficulty).
peri-megadim/4:ו: And what he wrote incident, etc. siman 443 Taz and Magen Avraham 5, 6 — exchanging chametz with others permitted; nevertheless specifically with great loss — here loss is slight, no advice; also lest the gentile sell to a Jew; see Mishna Lamelech chapter 5 of Laws of Marriage halacha 1 end s.v. general principle whether benefit prohibitions d'rabbanan forbidden to exchange oneself (see there); Rashi Chullin 4b explains Rabbanan also forbidden to exchange; if you say he explained to remove R' Yehuda's mind — they gain it is rabbinic; in Tosafot s.v. permitted one can say so; in Rosh Yosef I expanded there.
peri-megadim/4:ז: If they acquired chametz over which Passover passed from an apostate and did not know he was apostate, etc. — obvious mistaken transaction; see Mishna Lamelech chapter 5 halacha 7 (in Mishna Lamelech) and Laws of Sale chapter 16 halacha 14 and Yoreh De'ah 119:13; if the apostate wants to return money he may, for he takes his own as stated; see Yoreh De'ah siman 99 Shach letter 17 — I wrote in the name of one gaon an incident: bought immediately after Pesach certainly made on Pesach — only one barrel made after Pesach — one can say permitted to add and nullify (see there). Without great loss do not permit — there is double doubt to prohibition: perhaps halacha is like Rambam we do not add rabbinically; perhaps all was made.
peri-megadim/5:_: Perhaps. See Taz; Magen Avraham letter 6 — from Tur implies without "perhaps" and he promises if he wants he will take from him; Taz permits even to promise profit; on Olat Shabbat l'chatchila forbidden; the world is lenient as Taz wrote; see Eliyah Rabbah 12; without condition. If he sold chametz in the sixth hour to a gentile — one can say it is a sale and l'chatchila depends on dispute whether work helps; see Choshen Mishpat 207 and siman 208 in rabbinic too; see Kiddushin sold and betrothed with its value; see responsum Pnei Yehoshua Orach Chayim part 1 siman 12 and 14; above I brought it; see siman 431 in Shiyurei Knesset HaGedolah in responsa of rabbis of Venice. Nullification does not help at six — for absolute sale or he declares hefker in his domain.
peri-megadim/6:_: And even though. See Taz; Mesoret Binyamin siman 43 expanded — Magen Avraham brought (letter 5) because in everyone's mind he did not declare hefker. Forbidden to sue the gentile if he does not want — to sue he can sue the Jew who bought improperly. It appears one may sell the room and chametz for a large sum much above value and add as loan — in their law no concern for void sale; see Choshen Mishpat 227:26 — if so no one will give this sum. However from seif 3 selling for small amount no proof — there owners declare hefker and no void-sale concern (see Chak Yakov, Taz; Terumat HaDeshen 120). In any case here likewise one can say so; if slightly less than.
peri-megadim/7:ב: Partners gentile and Jew in chametz — after Pesach gentile's share permitted and Jew's forbidden, for in d'rabbanan there is clarification (Chak Yakov 2); see Eliyah Rabbah 1 who brought Yoreh De'ah 146:4 convert and gentile money and chametz, etc.; gentile who robbed Jew's chametz and Passover passed — Eliyah Rabbah leaned lenient; also incident gentile ground Jew's grain and baked on Pesach and brought after — leaned lenient; if Jew left wheat in mill and gentile came and said to Jew he will grind — see Chak Yakov letter 4 in the name of Chinuch Beit Yehuda siman 11 — many doubts lenient; casual speech possible intent the Jew will owe him a favor; possible even without that there is no gentile.
peri-megadim/7:ג: Incident: a Jew sold chametz to a gentile and said all in this room is yours; afterward another Jew came and gave this Jew chametz and left it there — requires study: if Jew 1 afterward gave for the sake of what was in his domain — permitted, for he told the gentile all found there is yours; unlike other chametz — one does not transfer what did not yet exist — requires study; see siman 446 Magen Avraham 1 and siman 449 Taz (5) thing not yet existing in chametz; gentile's courtyard — per view gentile from gentile becomes agent — one can say likewise courtyard (see siman 448; Chak Yakov there) understand.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Seif 1 chametz of a gentile; chametz of deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor over which Passover passed — see Mishbetzot Zahav in opening general 2 letter 2.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/4:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 4: but gentile to gentile makes an agent — likewise Rikanti Choshen Mishpat siman 188; but from words of Baal HaTanya brought in Beit Yosef Yoreh De'ah siman 169 and glosses there 11 — proven gentile to gentile does not become agent, as Tiferet Lemoshe there; see Beit Shmuel Even HaEzer siman 5; responsum Maharam Mintz siman 5 wrote: but gentile to gentile possibly there is agency.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/6:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 5: now too he violates — see Machaneh Ephraim Laws of Forbidden Foods chapter 8; Taz s.v. further applies.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/7:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 7: only because of chametz stringency forbidden in seif 7 dealing with primary law l'chatchila — forbidden by law lest the condition not be fulfilled and the chametz be the Jew's and he violate bal yera'eh; but b'dieved if he did and the condition was fulfilled, by law chametz permitted afterward; however one can say it is in his power to fulfill the condition — if the gentile does not return he can say I accept as if received — which helps l'chatchila in gift (end of his words); if so one can say even l'chatchila permitted — requires study.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: Non-Jew. Baer Heitev; and what he wrote in the name of Kaf HaChayyim — Jew and gentile partners — see responsum Sha'agat Aryeh siman 89 and 90 who wrote: if they divided after Pesach even though he did not sell to the gentile before Pesach, nevertheless the Jew's share is also permitted; see responsum Beit Efraim siman 46 on this; see Sha'agat Aryeh siman 91 — two Jewish partners, one sold his chametz to a gentile before Pesach wherever it was to the gentile and the other did not sell — after division the seller's share permitted and the non-seller's forbidden (see there).
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: Non-Jew. Baer Heitev; see responsum Beit Efraim siman 34 — one had malt in Vienna belonging to a gentile to make burnt wine; the gentile said he would make burnt wine on Pesach; on the eve he sold the malt properly and the gentile threw the malt into boiling water to make burnt wine; some doubt: since he did not inform the buyer the gentile would throw the grain into water, it would be mistaken sale. I raised that one should not void the sale for this; see there copied from manuscript of the gaon Baal Peri Yehoshua — his view is malt is hard chametz; explained there everything depends whether spoiled greatly until unfit for human food as explained siman 442 — then hard; and.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 5: but here if the gentile wants to fulfill, etc. — meaning perforce we do not say "since," etc. as his own — only when it is in his power to acquire we say it is as if he already acquired; unlike a matter not his and not in his power to acquire, only dependent on others — we do not say as his own; therefore if he returned after Pesach and the condition was fulfilled, permitted; nevertheless it appears l'chatchila obviously forbidden, lest the gentile not return and retroactively the chametz was the Jew's; only Radbaz came to give reason to forbid chametz after Pesach by law; on this Magen Avraham wrote this does not apply since he cannot acquire; nevertheless I lean Radbaz.
chok-yaakov/3:א: Forbidden in benefit. So in the Mishnah chapter Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 28); agreed by all poskim. One might say from Tosafot beginning of Beitzah 6 that chametz after Pesach is permitted in benefit — perhaps gentile's only; but that too is explicit Mishnah there in chapter 21.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: Seif 3. If he sold in what they write in a sale deed to a gentile "all my chametz I sell to you" — per Rambam and Semag to Choshen Mishpat siman 208 it does not work, since he does not specify a particular kind (see responsum).
